name of.definition: The word or words by which a person, place, or thing is known.
name of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'name' when identifying the entity.
examples: What is the name of this beautiful street?
I cannot remember the name of that actor.
name of.common_mistake: ❌ What is the name for this city? ➜ ✅ What is the name of this city?

member of.definition: An individual belonging to a group, organization, or society.
member of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'member' when indicating the organization or group.
examples: She has been an active member of the sports club for two years.
Every member of the team worked hard.
member of.common_mistake: ❌ He is a member in our club. ➜ ✅ He is a member of our club.

part of.definition: A piece or segment that belongs to a whole.
part of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'part' when specifying the larger whole.
examples: Reading daily is an essential part of language learning.
Engineers replaced a broken part of the machine.
part of.common_mistake: ❌ This is part from the plan. ➜ ✅ This is part of the plan.

kind of.definition: A class or category of things having common characteristics.
kind of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'kind'. Do NOT use 'from' or 'about'.
examples: What kind of music do you enjoy listening to?
This is a new kind of smartphone.
kind of.common_mistake: ❌ What kind from tea is this? ➜ ✅ What kind of tea is this?

sort of.definition: A category of things or people having common features.
sort of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'sort' when referring to type or category.
examples: What sort of work do you do?
They sell every sort of fresh fruit.
sort of.common_mistake: ❌ What sort for car do you drive? ➜ ✅ What sort of car do you drive?

lot of.definition: A large quantity or number of something.
lot of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'a lot' before nouns.
examples: There were a lot of people at the concert last night.
We need a lot of water for the journey.
lot of.common_mistake: ❌ There are a lot students here. ➜ ✅ There are a lot of students here.

cup of.definition: A small bowl-shaped container for drinking, or the amount it holds.
cup of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' when quantifying liquid contents in a container.
examples: Would you like a fresh cup of coffee?
She drank a hot cup of tea before sleeping.
cup of.common_mistake: ❌ Bring me a cup with tea. ➜ ✅ Bring me a cup of tea.

price of.definition: The amount of money expected or required in payment for something.
price of.grammar_rule: Use 'price of' before the item purchased.
examples: The price of gasoline increased sharply this month.
What is the price of a ticket to London?
price of.common_mistake: ❌ What is the price for this book? ➜ ✅ What is the price of this book?

reason for.definition: A cause, explanation, or justification for an event or action.
reason for.grammar_rule: Use 'reason FOR' + noun/gerund. Contrast with the conjunction phrase 'because OF'.
examples: What was the main reason for his absence yesterday?
She explained her reason for resigning.
reason for.common_mistake: ❌ What was the reason of his anger? ➜ ✅ What was the reason for his anger?
reason for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reason for the delay' ➔ Conjunction: 'delayed because of the rain'

need for.definition: A requirement or necessity for something.
need for.grammar_rule: The noun 'need FOR' takes 'for'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'need' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: There is an urgent need for healthcare reform.
We see no need for further delay.
need for.common_mistake: ❌ We have a need of more time. ➜ ✅ We have a need for more time.
need for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'there is a need FOR action' ➔ Verb: 'we need action' (no prep)

request for.definition: An act of asking politely or formally for something.
request for.grammar_rule: The noun 'request FOR' takes 'for'. Contrast with the verb 'request' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Management approved her request for extra funding.
Send your request for information via email.
request for.common_mistake: ❌ He made a request of help. ➜ ✅ He made a request for help.
request for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a request FOR assistance' ➔ Verb: 'request' (no prep)

love for.definition: An intense feeling of deep affection or strong liking.
love for.grammar_rule: Use 'love for' or 'love of'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'love' which takes NO preposition.
examples: His deep love for nature inspired his poetry.
She expressed her love of art.
love for.common_mistake: ❌ Her love to animals is boundless. ➜ ✅ Her love for animals is boundless.
love for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'her love FOR music' ➔ Verb: 'she loves music' (no prep)

hope for.definition: A feeling of expectation and desire for a particular thing to happen.
hope for.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'hope for' and verb 'hope' (hope for) take 'for'.
examples: The doctors gave us new hope for his recovery.
We have great hope for the future.
hope for.common_mistake: ❌ We have hope about success. ➜ ✅ We have hope for success.
hope for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'there is hope FOR recovery' ➔ Verb: 'hope'

care of.grammar_rule: Used in the fossilized idiom 'take care OF'. Contrast with verb 'take care of' or 'care'.
examples: Who will take care of your dog while you are away?
She takes great care of her elderly parents.
care of.common_mistake: ❌ Take care for your health. ➜ ✅ Take care of your health.
care of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun idiom: 'take care OF him' ➔ Verb: 'care' (care about / care for)

interest in.definition: The feeling of wanting to know or learn about something.
interest in.grammar_rule: The noun 'interest IN' takes 'in'. This matches the adjective 'interested in'.
examples: He has a keen interest in computer programming.
Her interest in photography started early.
interest in.common_mistake: ❌ She has an interest about music. ➜ ✅ She has an interest in music.
interest in.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'take an interest IN science' ➔ Adjective: 'interested in'

belief in.definition: An acceptance that something exists or is true, especially without proof.
belief in.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'belief IN' and verb 'believe in' take 'in'.
examples: Her strong belief in justice guided her career.
He maintained a firm belief in his team's potential.
belief in.common_mistake: ❌ Belief on magic is common in fairy tales. ➜ ✅ Belief in magic is common in fairy tales.

trip to.definition: A journey or excursion to a place.
trip to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'trip' when specifying a travel destination.
examples: We are planning a weekend trip to Paris.
How was your recent trip to the mountains?
trip to.common_mistake: ❌ Our trip in Rome was wonderful. ➜ ✅ Our trip to Rome was wonderful.

visit to.definition: An act of going to see a person or place as a guest or tourist.
visit to.grammar_rule: The noun 'visit TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'visit' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: During our visit to London, we saw Big Ben.
He paid a short visit to his grandmother.
visit to.common_mistake: ❌ Our visit in the hospital was brief. ➜ ✅ Our visit to the hospital was brief.
visit to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a visit TO the museum' ➔ Verb: 'visit' (no prep)

way to.definition: A method, style, or route for reaching a place or achieving an object.
way to.grammar_rule: Use 'way to' before destinations or goals.
examples: Can you tell me the best way to the train station?
Hard work is the surest way to success.
way to.common_mistake: ❌ What is the way for the beach? ➜ ✅ What is the way to the beach?

key to.definition: A small metal instrument for operating a lock, OR a crucial element for success.
key to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'key' for both physical locks and figurative solutions/success.
examples: Do you have the key to the front door?
Education is the key to personal development.
key to.common_mistake: ❌ Where is the key for my car? ➜ ✅ Where is the key to my car?

answer to.definition: A spoken or written reaction to a question, test, or problem.
answer to.grammar_rule: The noun 'answer TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'answer' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Nobody knew the correct answer to the teacher's question.
We are still awaiting an answer to our email.
answer to.common_mistake: ❌ What is the answer for number 3? ➜ ✅ What is the answer to number 3?
answer to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the answer TO your question' ➔ Verb: 'answer' (no prep)

letter to.definition: A written message addressed to a person or organization.
letter to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'letter' when specifying the recipient.
examples: She wrote a heartfelt letter to her childhood friend.
I received a formal letter to the bank manager.
letter to.common_mistake: ❌ Send a letter for the embassy. ➜ ✅ Send a letter to the embassy.
letter to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'write a letter TO her' ➔ Verb: 'write to'

invitation to.definition: A written or spoken request inviting someone to attend an event.
invitation to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'invitation'. Do NOT use 'for'.
examples: Did you receive an invitation to Sarah's wedding?
Thank you for the kind invitation to dinner.
invitation to.common_mistake: ❌ An invitation for the party arrived today. ➜ ✅ An invitation to the party arrived today.

picture of.definition: A painting, drawing, or photograph representing a person or scene.
picture of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'picture' or 'photo' to indicate the subject depicted.
examples: She showed me a lovely picture of her new puppy.
This is a famous picture of the Eiffel Tower.
picture of.common_mistake: ❌ Here is a picture from my family. ➜ ✅ Here is a picture of my family.

photo of.definition: A photograph representing someone or something.
examples: He took a stunning photo of the sunset over the ocean.
Send me a photo of your new apartment.
photo of.common_mistake: ❌ Can I see a photo from your trip? ➜ ✅ Can I see a photo of your trip?

map of.definition: A diagrammatic representation of an area of land or sea.
map of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'map' when identifying the geographical area.
examples: Do you have a street map of central London?
The tour guide handed us a map of the national park.
map of.common_mistake: ❌ Here is a map for the subway. ➜ ✅ Here is a map of the subway.

group of.definition: A number of people or things gathered or located together.
group of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after collective nouns like 'group'.
examples: A large group of tourists arrived at the museum.
The teacher addressed a group of concerned parents.
group of.common_mistake: ❌ A group from students stood outside. ➜ ✅ A group of students stood outside.

glass of.definition: A drinking vessel made of glass, or its contents.
glass of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' when quantifying contents in a glass.
examples: May I have a cold glass of water, please?
He poured a glass of orange juice with breakfast.
glass of.common_mistake: ❌ A glass with milk, please. ➜ ✅ A glass of milk, please.

piece of.pattern: piece of + [uncountable noun / cake / advice / paper]
piece of.definition: A portion of an item or an instance of an uncountable noun.
piece of.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' in partitive expressions like 'piece of'.
examples: Let me give you a useful piece of advice.
Would you like another piece of chocolate cake?
piece of.common_mistake: ❌ A piece from paper. ➜ ✅ A piece of paper.

slice of.definition: A thin, broad piece cut from something.
examples: He ate three slices of pizza for lunch.
Add a slice of lemon to my tea.
slice of.common_mistake: ❌ A slice from bread. ➜ ✅ A slice of bread.

cost of.definition: The amount that has to be paid or spent to buy or obtain something.
cost of.grammar_rule: Use 'cost of' before the item, service, or concept.
examples: The cost of living in major cities has risen sharply.
What is the total cost of repairs?
cost of.common_mistake: ❌ What is the cost for this project? ➜ ✅ What is the cost of this project?

ticket to.definition: A printed piece of paper giving the holder a right to enter a place or travel.
ticket to.grammar_rule: Use 'ticket to' a place or event (ticket to Paris / ticket to the concert). 'Ticket for' is also used for events.
examples: I bought two tickets to the theater performance.
Where can I buy a ticket for the football match?
ticket to.common_mistake: ❌ I need a ticket at Rome. ➜ ✅ I need a ticket to Rome.

gift for.definition: A thing given willingly to someone without payment; a present.
gift for.grammar_rule: Use 'gift for' when specifying the recipient.
examples: I bought a lovely birthday gift for my mother.
This watch is a gift for your hard work.
gift for.common_mistake: ❌ A gift to my friend (from me). ➜ ✅ A gift for my friend.

time for.definition: An appointed or suitable moment for something.
time for.grammar_rule: Use 'time for' before nouns or gerunds (time for bed / time for lunch).
examples: It is time for lunch!
There is no time for hesitation now.
time for.common_mistake: ❌ It is time to the meeting. ➜ ✅ It is time for the meeting.

place for.definition: A particular position, point, or area suitable for a purpose.
place for.grammar_rule: Use 'place for' when assigning function or location.
examples: There is a special place for books on the shelf.
A hospital is a place for healing.
place for.common_mistake: ❌ A place to store tools. ➜ ✅ A place for storing tools.

work of.definition: A literary or artistic creation, or labor by someone.
work of.grammar_rule: Use 'work of' when attributing artistic or creative origin.
examples: Mona Lisa is a world-famous work of art.
This novel is the masterpiece work of Tolstoy.
work of.common_mistake: ❌ A work from Picasso. ➜ ✅ A work of Picasso.

attention to.definition: Notice taken of someone or something; regarding someone as interesting or important.
examples: Please pay close attention to the safety demonstration.
She turned her attention to her new project.
attention to.common_mistake: ❌ Pay attention at the teacher. ➜ ✅ Pay attention to the teacher.
attention to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'pay attention TO the speaker' ➔ Verb: 'listen to'

access to.definition: The means or opportunity to approach or enter a place.
access to.grammar_rule: The noun 'access TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'access' which takes NO preposition.
examples: All employees have access to the company database.
Does this room have wheelchair access to the garden?
access to.common_mistake: ❌ We have access for the library. ➜ ✅ We have access to the library.
access to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'have access TO the file' ➔ Verb: 'access the file' (no prep)

approach to.definition: A way of dealing with something or a way of doing something.
approach to.grammar_rule: The noun 'approach TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'approach' which takes NO preposition.
examples: We need a fresh approach to solving this technical problem.
Her approach to teaching is very interactive.
approach to.common_mistake: ❌ What is your approach for this project? ➜ ✅ What is your approach to this project?
approach to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'our approach TO learning' ➔ Verb: 'approach the problem' (no prep)

solution to.definition: A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
solution to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'solution' when identifying the problem resolved.
examples: Engineers found a simple solution to the water leakage issue.
There is no quick solution to climate change.
solution to.common_mistake: ❌ We need a solution for this error. ➜ ✅ We need a solution to this error.
solution to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a solution TO the crisis' ➔ Verb: 'solve the crisis' (no prep)

reaction to.definition: An action performed or feeling experienced in response to a situation or event.
reaction to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'reaction' to identify the stimulus.
examples: What was his initial reaction to the proposal?
She suffered an allergic reaction to the medication.
reaction to.common_mistake: ❌ Her reaction for the movie was unexpected. ➜ ✅ Her reaction to the movie was unexpected.
reaction to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reaction TO the news' ➔ Verb: 'react to'

response to.definition: A verbal or written answer, or a reaction to something.
examples: We received a swift response to our complaint letter.
In response to customer feedback, we changed the menu.
response to.common_mistake: ❌ Here is my response for your question. ➜ ✅ Here is my response to your question.
response to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'response TO our email' ➔ Verb: 'answer' (no prep)

contribution to.definition: A gift or payment to a common fund, or an effort that helps bring about a result.
contribution to.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'contribution TO' and verb 'contribute to' take 'to'.
examples: He made a significant financial contribution to the hospital.
Her research was a valuable contribution to science.
contribution to.common_mistake: ❌ Thank you for your contribution for our team. ➜ ✅ Thank you for your contribution to our team.

damage to.definition: Physical harm caused to something in such a way as to impair its value, usefulness, or normal function.
damage to.grammar_rule: The noun 'damage TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'damage' which takes NO preposition.
examples: The storm caused severe damage to several coastal homes.
Smoking causes long-term damage to your health.
damage to.common_mistake: ❌ The accident caused damage of my car. ➜ ✅ The accident caused damage to my car.
damage to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'damage TO the vehicle' ➔ Verb: 'damage the vehicle' (no prep)

threat to.definition: A person or thing likely to cause damage or danger.
threat to.grammar_rule: Use 'threat TO' when identifying the vulnerable target.
examples: Pollution poses a serious threat to marine ecosystems.
Cyber attacks are a growing threat to business continuity.
threat to.common_mistake: ❌ Climate change is a threat for wildlife. ➜ ✅ Climate change is a threat to wildlife.
threat to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'threat TO security' ➔ Verb: 'threaten security' (no prep)

alternative to.definition: One of two or more available possibilities.
alternative to.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'alternative' when specifying what is being replaced.
examples: Cycling is a healthy alternative to driving to work.
We are looking for an alternative to fossil fuels.
alternative to.common_mistake: ❌ Is there an alternative for this method? ➜ ✅ Is there an alternative to this method?

relationship with.definition: The way in which two or more people or things are connected.
relationship with.grammar_rule: Use 'relationship WITH' a person, and 'relationship BETWEEN' two entities.
examples: She has a wonderful relationship with her mother.
We need to examine the relationship between diet and health.
relationship with.common_mistake: ❌ What is your relationship to him? ➜ ✅ What is your relationship with him?

connection with.definition: A relationship in which a person, thing, or idea is linked or associated with something else.
examples: Is there any connection with the previous case?
Police questioned him in connection with the robbery.
connection with.common_mistake: ❌ There is no connection for these events. ➜ ✅ There is no connection between these events.

contact with.definition: The state or condition of physical touching or communication.
contact with.grammar_rule: The noun 'contact WITH' takes 'with'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'contact' which takes NO preposition.
examples: Avoid direct contact with hazardous chemicals.
I am still in close contact with my university classmates.
contact with.common_mistake: ❌ I made contact to the client. ➜ ✅ I made contact with the client.
contact with.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'keep in contact WITH me' ➔ Verb: 'contact me' (no prep)

difficulty with.definition: The state or condition of being difficult; effort required.
difficulty with.grammar_rule: Use 'difficulty WITH' a noun/task, and 'difficulty IN' + gerund (-ing).
examples: He experiences difficulty with English pronunciation.
She had great difficulty in finding an apartment.
difficulty with.common_mistake: ❌ I have difficulty to understand this rule. ➜ ✅ I have difficulty in understanding this rule.

problem with.definition: A matter or situation regarded as unwelcome or harmful and needing to be dealt with.
problem with.grammar_rule: Always use 'with' after 'problem' when specifying the source of trouble.
examples: There is a technical problem with the server right now.
What is the problem with your bicycle?
problem with.common_mistake: ❌ I have a problem of my computer. ➜ ✅ I have a problem with my computer.

experience of.definition: Practical contact with and observation of facts or events.
experience of.grammar_rule: Use 'experience OF' an event, and 'experience IN' a field or job.
examples: Do you have any prior experience in software sales?
It was an unforgettable experience of mountain climbing.
experience of.common_mistake: ❌ She has experience about managing projects. ➜ ✅ She has experience in managing projects.

increase in.definition: A rise in the amount, size, or degree of something.
increase in.grammar_rule: Use 'increase IN' before the concept rising (e.g. increase in sales). Contrast with 'increase BY' for the amount (increased by 10%).
examples: There has been a sharp increase in house prices.
We noticed an increase in website traffic.
increase in.common_mistake: ❌ An increase of the price. ➜ ✅ An increase in the price.
increase in.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an increase IN sales' ➔ Verb: 'sales increased by 10%'

decrease in.definition: A process of becoming smaller or fewer.
decrease in.grammar_rule: Use 'decrease IN' before the subject dropping.
examples: The company reported a decrease in quarterly revenue.
A gradual decrease in temperature signals autumn.
decrease in.common_mistake: ❌ A decrease of unemployment. ➜ ✅ A decrease in unemployment.

rise in.definition: An increase in number, size, amount, or quality.
rise in.grammar_rule: Always use 'IN' after 'rise' before the fluctuating noun.
examples: The rise in sea levels threatens coastal areas.
Employees welcomed the rise in minimum wage.
rise in.common_mistake: ❌ A rise of cost. ➜ ✅ A rise in cost.

fall in.definition: A decrease in size, quantity, or value.
fall in.grammar_rule: Use 'fall IN' before the metric dropping.
examples: A sudden fall in gas prices surprised analysts.
The fall in unemployment is encouraging news.
fall in.common_mistake: ❌ A fall of inflation. ➜ ✅ A fall in inflation.

participation in.definition: The action of taking part in something.
participation in.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'participation IN' and verb 'participate in' take 'in'.
examples: Student participation in classroom discussions is encouraged.
Thank you for your active participation in the workshop.
participation in.common_mistake: ❌ Participation on the seminar was high. ➜ ✅ Participation in the seminar was high.

confidence in.definition: The feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something.
confidence in.grammar_rule: Use 'confidence IN' a person or system. Contrast with adjective 'confident about'.
examples: Voters lost confidence in the local government.
I have full confidence in your abilities.
confidence in.common_mistake: ❌ She has confidence about her team. ➜ ✅ She has confidence in her team.
confidence in.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'have confidence IN him' ➔ Adjective: 'confident about'

faith in.definition: Complete trust or confidence in someone or something.
faith in.grammar_rule: Always use 'IN' after 'faith'. Contrast with adjective 'faithful to'.
examples: She never lost her faith in humanity.
His faith in science motivated his research.
faith in.common_mistake: ❌ Have faith to yourself. ➜ ✅ Have faith in yourself.
faith in.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'have faith IN justice' ➔ Adjective: 'faithful to'

benefit of.definition: An advantage or profit gained from something.
benefit of.grammar_rule: Use 'benefit OF' when listing an intrinsic advantage. Contrast with verb 'benefit from'.
examples: What are the health benefits of eating vegetables?
One benefit of remote work is saving commute time.
benefit of.common_mistake: ❌ The benefit for drinking water. ➜ ✅ The benefit of drinking water.
benefit of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the benefit OF exercise' ➔ Verb: 'benefit from'

advantage of.definition: A condition or circumstance that puts one in a favorable position.
advantage of.grammar_rule: Use 'advantage OF' a feature, and 'advantage OVER' a rival.
examples: The main advantage of solar energy is that it is renewable.
Our team has a distinct advantage over the opponents.
advantage of.common_mistake: ❌ An advantage for living here. ➜ ✅ An advantage of living here.

disadvantage of.definition: An unfavorable circumstance or condition that reduces success.
examples: A major disadvantage of living downtown is noise pollution.
Consider the disadvantages of taking a loan.
disadvantage of.common_mistake: ❌ The disadvantage for buying cheap shoes. ➜ ✅ The disadvantage of buying cheap shoes.

cause of.definition: A person or thing that gives rise to an action, phenomenon, or condition.
cause of.grammar_rule: Always use 'cause OF' for a noun. Contrast with 'reason FOR'.
examples: Investigators determined the cause of the electrical fire.
Stress is a leading cause of heart illness.
cause of.common_mistake: ❌ What was the cause for the accident? ➜ ✅ What was the cause of the accident?
cause of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the cause OF the fire' ➔ Noun contrast: 'the reason FOR the decision'

result of.definition: A consequence, effect, or outcome of something.
result of.grammar_rule: Use 'result OF' as a noun. Contrast with verb 'result from'.
examples: The high test scores were the direct result of hard work.
He suffered injuries as a result of the collision.
result of.common_mistake: ❌ As a result from the storm, power failed. ➜ ✅ As a result of the storm, power failed.
result of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the result OF the study' ➔ Verb: 'result from'

lack of.definition: The state of being without or not having enough of something.
lack of.grammar_rule: The noun 'lack OF' takes 'of'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'lack' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: The project failed due to a lack of proper funding.
Her main issue is a lack of experience.
lack of.common_mistake: ❌ He has a lack for enthusiasm. ➜ ✅ He has a lack of enthusiasm.
lack of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a lack OF confidence' ➔ Verb: 'lack' (no prep)

shortage of.definition: A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained in sufficient amounts.
shortage of.grammar_rule: Always use 'OF' after 'shortage'. Contrast with adjective 'short of'.
examples: The city is facing a severe shortage of affordable housing.
Drought caused a shortage of fresh vegetables.
shortage of.common_mistake: ❌ There is a shortage for skilled labor. ➜ ✅ There is a shortage of skilled labor.
shortage of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a shortage OF water' ➔ Adjective: 'short of'

demand for.definition: The desire of purchasers, consumers, or clients for a commodity or service.
demand for.grammar_rule: The noun 'demand FOR' takes 'for'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'demand' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: There is a growing demand for renewable energy technology.
High demand for tickets crashed the website.
demand for.common_mistake: ❌ The demand of organic food is rising. ➜ ✅ The demand for organic food is rising.
demand for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'high demand FOR energy' ➔ Verb: 'demand' (no prep)

respect for.definition: A feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities or qualities.
respect for.grammar_rule: Use 'respect FOR' people or rules. Contrast with adjective 'respectful to'.
examples: Children should learn respect for others.
He showed great respect for his elders.
respect for.common_mistake: ❌ Show respect to the rules. ➜ ✅ Show respect for the rules.
respect for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'respect FOR the law' ➔ Adjective: 'respectful to'

concern for.definition: Anxiety or worry, or a feeling of sympathy.
concern for.grammar_rule: Use 'concern FOR' someone's welfare, and 'concern ABOUT' an issue.
examples: The doctor expressed deep concern for the patient's condition.
Public concern about climate change is growing.
concern for.common_mistake: ❌ Concern of safety. ➜ ✅ Concern for safety.

sympathy for.definition: Feelings of pity and sorrow for someone else's misfortune.
sympathy for.grammar_rule: The noun takes 'sympathy FOR'. Contrast with adjective 'sympathetic to'.
examples: We feel great sympathy for the families affected by the flood.
He expressed sympathy for his grieving colleague.
sympathy for.common_mistake: ❌ Sympathy to the poor. ➜ ✅ Sympathy for the poor.
sympathy for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'sympathy FOR the victims' ➔ Adjective: 'sympathetic to'

examples: I have tremendous admiration for her courage and determination.
His honesty earned him the admiration of all.
admiration for.common_mistake: ❌ Admiration to his work. ➜ ✅ Admiration for his work.

habit of.definition: A settled or regular tendency or practice.
examples: She has a healthy habit of drinking water every morning.
Don't get into the bad habit of procrastination.
habit of.common_mistake: ❌ The habit to bite nails. ➜ ✅ The habit of biting nails.

effect on.definition: A change which is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.
effect on.grammar_rule: The noun 'effect ON' takes 'on'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'affect' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Pollution has a devastating effect on human health.
What effect will this law have on small businesses?
effect on.common_mistake: ❌ It has an effect in my decision. ➜ ✅ It has an effect on my decision.
effect on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an effect ON health' ➔ Verb: 'affect' (no prep)

impact on.grammar_rule: The noun 'impact ON' takes 'on'. Contrast with verb 'impact' (often direct object in formal prose).
examples: Technology has had a huge impact on modern communication.
Scientists studied the asteroid's impact on climate.
impact on.common_mistake: ❌ It has an impact to our community. ➜ ✅ It has an impact on our community.
impact on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an impact ON the economy' ➔ Verb: 'impact'

influence on.definition: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
influence on.grammar_rule: The noun 'influence ON' takes 'on'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'influence' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Parents have a profound influence on their children's values.
His musical style was a strong influence on jazz.
influence on.common_mistake: ❌ He has an influence over me. ➜ ✅ He has an influence on me.
influence on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'have an influence ON children' ➔ Verb: 'influence' (no prep)

criticism of.definition: The expression of disapproval of someone or something based on perceived faults.
criticism of.grammar_rule: The noun 'criticism OF' takes 'of'. Matches adjective 'critical of'.
examples: The government faced severe criticism of its economic policy.
Constructive criticism of your work helps you grow.
criticism of.common_mistake: ❌ Criticism about his conduct. ➜ ✅ Criticism of his conduct.
criticism of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'criticism OF the policy' ➔ Adjective: 'critical of'

ban on.grammar_rule: Always use 'BAN ON' when specifying prohibited items or activities.
examples: The city announced a complete ban on single-use plastic bags.
There is a strict ban on parking along this street.
ban on.common_mistake: ❌ A ban for firearms. ➜ ✅ A ban on firearms.

tax on.definition: A compulsory contribution to state revenue.
tax on.grammar_rule: Always use 'tax ON' before taxed goods or income.
examples: The government introduced a higher tax on luxury imported cars.
A tax on sugary drinks aims to improve public health.
tax on.common_mistake: ❌ A tax for sugar. ➜ ✅ A tax on sugar.

effect of.definition: The outcome or result produced by a specific cause.
effect of.grammar_rule: Use 'effect OF' when highlighting the agent causing the change (effect of light).
examples: Researchers studied the long-term effects of sleep deprivation.
The effect of the new medicine was almost immediate.
effect of.common_mistake: ❌ The effect from the drug. ➜ ✅ The effect of the drug.

dependence on.definition: The state of relying on or being controlled by someone or something.
dependence on.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'depend' (depend on) and adjective 'dependent on'.
examples: Reducing our dependence on foreign oil is a national priority.
Childhood involves total dependence on parents.
dependence on.common_mistake: ❌ Dependence from computers. ➜ ✅ Dependence on computers.
dependence on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'dependence ON fossil fuels' ➔ Verb: 'depend' ➔ Adjective: 'dependent on'

reliance on.definition: Dependence on or trust in someone or something.
reliance on.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'rely on' and adjective 'reliant on'.
examples: Heavy reliance on automated tools can lead to skill loss.
Their reliance on seasonal labor caused problems.
reliance on.common_mistake: ❌ Reliance to imports. ➜ ✅ Reliance on imports.
reliance on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reliance ON public transit' ➔ Verb: 'rely on' ➔ Adjective: 'reliant on'

agreement with.definition: A negotiated and typically legally binding arrangement between parties.
agreement with.grammar_rule: Use 'agreement WITH' a partner, and 'agreement ON' a topic.
examples: We reached a formal agreement with our suppliers yesterday.
Is there general agreement on the new guidelines?
agreement with.common_mistake: ❌ An agreement to the client. ➜ ✅ An agreement with the client.
agreement with.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reach an agreement WITH them' ➔ Verb: 'agree with'

apology for.definition: A regretful acknowledgment of an offense or failure.
apology for.grammar_rule: Use 'apology FOR' an action. Use 'apology TO' a person.
examples: He offered a sincere apology for his rude comment.
Please accept my apology for the delay.
apology for.common_mistake: ❌ An apology about my mistake. ➜ ✅ An apology for my mistake.
apology for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an apology FOR being late' ➔ Verb: 'apologize to'

objection to.definition: An expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition.
objection to.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'object to'. The 'to' is a preposition requiring a noun or gerund.
examples: Does anyone have any objection to moving the meeting to Friday?
The lawyer raised an objection to the question.
objection to.common_mistake: ❌ An objection for the idea. ➜ ✅ An objection to the idea.
objection to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an objection TO the plan' ➔ Verb: 'object to'

dedication to.definition: The quality of being committed to a task or purpose.
dedication to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'dedicated to'. Followed by noun or gerund.
examples: Her dedication to teaching earned her a national award.
We admire his total dedication to his family.
dedication to.common_mistake: ❌ Dedication for medicine. ➜ ✅ Dedication to medicine.
dedication to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'dedication TO public service' ➔ Adjective: 'dedicated to'

commitment to.definition: The state or quality of being dedicated to a cause or activity.
commitment to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'committed to'. Followed by noun or gerund.
examples: The company demonstrated a firm commitment to environmental safety.
Marriage requires a long-term commitment to one another.
commitment to.common_mistake: ❌ A commitment for excellence. ➜ ✅ A commitment to excellence.

addiction to.definition: The fact or condition of being addicted to a particular substance or activity.
examples: His addiction to online gambling ruined his finances.
Screen addiction to phones affects teenagers.
addiction to.common_mistake: ❌ Addiction for alcohol. ➜ ✅ Addiction to alcohol.

preference for.definition: A greater liking for one alternative over another.
preference for.grammar_rule: Use 'preference FOR' a choice, or 'preference OVER' an alternative.
examples: She expressed a clear preference for working from home.
Consumers have a preference for organic products.
preference for.common_mistake: ❌ A preference to tea instead of coffee. ➜ ✅ A preference for tea instead of coffee.

reputation for.definition: The beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something.
reputation for.grammar_rule: Use 'reputation FOR' a characteristic. Contrast with adjective 'famous for'.
examples: The university has an international reputation for research excellence.
He has a reputation for being punctual.
reputation for.common_mistake: ❌ A reputation of honesty. ➜ ✅ A reputation for honesty.
reputation for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a reputation FOR reliability' ➔ Adjective: 'famous for'

responsibility for.definition: The state or fact of having a duty to deal with something or having control over someone.
responsibility for.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'responsible for'. Use 'responsibility FOR' a duty.
examples: He accepted full responsibility for the accident.
Managing safety is the responsibility of the supervisor.
responsibility for.common_mistake: ❌ Responsibility to manage the team. ➜ ✅ Responsibility for managing the team.
responsibility for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'take responsibility FOR the error' ➔ Adjective: 'responsible for'

danger of.definition: The possibility of suffering harm or injury.
danger of.grammar_rule: Use 'danger OF' before a risk event or gerund. Contrast with adjective 'dangerous for'.
examples: Drivers were warned about the danger of ice on the roads.
Is there any danger of an explosion?
danger of.common_mistake: ❌ The danger for slipping. ➜ ✅ The danger of slipping.
danger of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the danger OF collapse' ➔ Adjective: 'dangerous for'

doubt about.definition: A feeling of uncertainty or lack of conviction.
examples: I have serious doubts about the accuracy of his report.
There is no doubt about her technical ability.
doubt about.common_mistake: ❌ Doubts for his honesty. ➜ ✅ Doubts about his honesty.

suspicion of.definition: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true.
examples: He was arrested on suspicion of tax evasion.
Her sudden wealth aroused suspicion among neighbors.
suspicion of.common_mistake: ❌ Suspicion for murder. ➜ ✅ Suspicion of murder.

awareness of.definition: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.
awareness of.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'aware of'. Always use 'awareness OF'.
examples: The campaign aims to raise public awareness of mental health issues.
She has an acute awareness of her surroundings.
awareness of.common_mistake: ❌ Awareness about safety. ➜ ✅ Awareness of safety.
awareness of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'raise awareness OF diabetes' ➔ Adjective: 'aware of'

knowledge of.definition: Facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education.
knowledge of.grammar_rule: Always use 'knowledge OF' a topic or language.
examples: Candidates must possess a working knowledge of French.
His knowledge of world history is impressive.
knowledge of.common_mistake: ❌ Knowledge about biology. ➜ ✅ Knowledge of biology.

understanding of.definition: The ability to understand something; comprehension.
examples: This textbook provides a clear understanding of economics.
We share a mutual understanding of the rules.
understanding of.common_mistake: ❌ Understanding for mathematics. ➜ ✅ Understanding of mathematics.

impression of.definition: An idea, feeling, or opinion of something or someone, formed without conscious thought.
examples: What was your first impression of the new manager?
The city left a lasting impression of elegance on us.
impression of.common_mistake: ❌ My impression about Paris. ➜ ✅ My impression of Paris.

opinion of.definition: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact.
opinion of.grammar_rule: Use 'opinion OF' a person's character, and 'opinion ON/ABOUT' a controversial issue.
examples: What is your honest opinion of his performance?
Public opinion on climate policy is divided.
opinion of.common_mistake: ❌ An opinion for this matter. ➜ ✅ An opinion on this matter.

attitude toward.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling about someone or something.
examples: Her positive attitude toward work inspires the team.
Changes in societal attitudes to marriage have occurred.
attitude toward.common_mistake: ❌ An attitude for learning. ➜ ✅ An attitude toward learning.

exception to.definition: A person or thing that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule.
exception to.grammar_rule: Always use 'exception TO' a rule. Do NOT use 'of' or 'for'.
examples: There is an exception to every rule.
We cannot make an exception to our security policy.
exception to.common_mistake: ❌ An exception of the law. ➜ ✅ An exception to the law.

addition to.definition: A person or thing added to something else.
examples: This book is a valuable addition to our library.
They welcomed a new addition to their family.
addition to.common_mistake: ❌ An addition for the collection. ➜ ✅ An addition to the collection.

exception from.definition: Exemption or relief from a general burden.
exception from.grammar_rule: Use 'exception FROM' when exempted from a duty.
examples: He requested an exception from mandatory training.
Exemption from service was granted.
exception from.common_mistake: ❌ Exception to military service. ➜ ✅ Exemption from military service.

contrast to.definition: The state of being strikingly different from something else in juxtaposition.
contrast to.grammar_rule: Use 'in contrast TO' or 'in contrast WITH'. Contrast with adjective 'different from'.
examples: His quiet nature was a sharp contrast to his energetic brother.
In contrast to expectations, profits fell.
contrast to.common_mistake: ❌ In contrast from last week. ➜ ✅ In contrast to last week.
contrast to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'in contrast TO last year' ➔ Adjective: 'different from'

similarity to.definition: The state or fact of being similar; resemblance.
similarity to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'similar to'. Always use 'similarity TO'.
examples: The painting bears an uncanny similarity to a Rembrandt masterpiece.
There is little similarity to the original draft.
similarity to.common_mistake: ❌ Similarity with the original. ➜ ✅ Similarity to the original.
similarity to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'similarity TO her mother' ➔ Adjective: 'similar to'

difference between.definition: A point or way in which things or people are not the same.
difference between.grammar_rule: Use 'difference BETWEEN' two entities. Contrast with adjective 'different from'.
examples: What is the main difference between these two software versions?
There is a noticeable difference in quality.
difference between.common_mistake: ❌ The difference from option A and B. ➜ ✅ The difference between option A and B.
difference between.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the difference BETWEEN the two' ➔ Adjective: 'different from'

search for.definition: An act of searching for someone or something.
search for.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'search FOR' and verb 'search' (search for) take 'for'.
examples: Police expanded their search for the missing hiker.
Her search for employment took three months.
search for.common_mistake: ❌ A search of solution. ➜ ✅ A search for a solution.
search for.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the search FOR evidence' ➔ Verb: 'search' (search for)

desire for.definition: A strong feeling of wanting to have something or wishing for something to happen.
examples: Her intense desire for knowledge drove her studies.
He showed no desire for power.
desire for.common_mistake: ❌ A desire of money. ➜ ✅ A desire for money.

enthusiasm for.definition: Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.
enthusiasm for.grammar_rule: Use 'enthusiasm FOR' a subject. Contrast with adjective 'excited about' or 'keen on'.
examples: The team showed immense enthusiasm for the new project.
Her enthusiasm for teaching never faded.
enthusiasm for.common_mistake: ❌ Enthusiasm about learning. ➜ ✅ Enthusiasm for learning.

resistance to.definition: The refusal to accept or comply with something; the ability not to be affected by something.
resistance to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'resistant to'. Always use 'resistance TO'.
examples: There was strong public resistance to the new tax law.
Bacteria can develop resistance to antibiotics.
resistance to.common_mistake: ❌ Resistance against change. ➜ ✅ Resistance to change.

susceptibility to.definition: The state or fact of being likely or liable to be influenced or harmed by a particular thing.
susceptibility to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'susceptible to'. Always use 'susceptibility TO'.
examples: Malnutrition increases susceptibility to viral infections.
Her emotional susceptibility to criticism was evident.
susceptibility to.common_mistake: ❌ Susceptibility for disease. ➜ ✅ Susceptibility to disease.

immunity to.definition: Resistance to a disease or protection from legal burden.
immunity to.grammar_rule: Use 'immunity TO' diseases, and 'immunity FROM' prosecution.
examples: Vaccines build long-term immunity to contagious diseases.
The witness was granted immunity from prosecution.
immunity to.common_mistake: ❌ Immunity against prosecution. ➜ ✅ Immunity from prosecution.

vulnerability to.definition: The quality or state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed.
examples: The report highlighted the island's vulnerability to extreme weather.
Cybersecurity audits reveal vulnerability to hacking.
vulnerability to.common_mistake: ❌ Vulnerability for stress. ➜ ✅ Vulnerability to stress.

indifference to.definition: Lack of interest, concern, or sympathy.
examples: His callous indifference to the feelings of others shocked everyone.
Consumer indifference to advertising is rising.
indifference to.common_mistake: ❌ Indifference about politics. ➜ ✅ Indifference to politics.

incompatibility with.definition: The state of two things being so different as to be incapable of existing together.
examples: Software incompatibility with the operating system caused crashes.
Marital incompatibility led to divorce.
incompatibility with.common_mistake: ❌ Incompatibility to old versions. ➜ ✅ Incompatibility with old versions.
incompatibility with.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'incompatibility WITH company culture' ➔ Adjective: 'incompatible with'

inconsistency with.definition: The fact or state of being inconsistent.
inconsistency with.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'inconsistent with' and contrast 'consistent with'.
examples: Lawyers pointed out an inconsistency with his previous statement.
Quality inconsistency with factory standards was noted.
inconsistency with.common_mistake: ❌ Inconsistency to the truth. ➜ ✅ Inconsistency with the truth.
inconsistency with.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'inconsistency WITH the evidence' ➔ Adjective: 'consistent with'

adherence to.definition: Attachment or commitment to a person, cause, or belief.
adherence to.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'adhere to'. Always use 'adherence TO'.
examples: Strict adherence to protocol prevented accidents.
Religious adherence to traditional customs.
adherence to.common_mistake: ❌ Adherence with rules. ➜ ✅ Adherence to rules.
adherence to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'adherence TO safety regulations' ➔ Verb: 'adhere to'

conformity to.definition: Behavior in accordance with socially accepted conventions or standards.
conformity to.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'conform to'. Use 'conformity TO' or 'conformity WITH'.
examples: Pressure for conformity to group expectations is strong among peers.
In conformity with regulations, we submitted the report.
conformity to.common_mistake: ❌ Conformity for standards. ➜ ✅ Conformity to standards.
conformity to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'conformity TO social norms' ➔ Verb: 'conform to'

compliance with.definition: The action or fact of complying with a wish or command.
compliance with.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'comply with'. Always use 'compliance WITH'.
examples: The company demonstrated full compliance with safety standards.
Non-compliance with tax rules carries severe fines.
compliance with.common_mistake: ❌ Compliance to the regulations. ➜ ✅ Compliance with the regulations.
compliance with.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'compliance WITH environmental law' ➔ Verb: 'comply with'

infringement on.definition: The action of breaking the terms of a law or agreement, or encroaching on rights.
infringement on.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'infringe on'. Use 'infringement ON/UPON' (or 'infringement OF copyright').
examples: Surveillance laws represent an infringement on personal privacy.
The company faced lawsuits for copyright infringement.
infringement on.common_mistake: ❌ Infringement against rights. ➜ ✅ Infringement on rights.
infringement on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'infringement ON civil liberties' ➔ Verb: 'infringe on'

disregard for.definition: The action or state of paying no attention to something.
disregard for.grammar_rule: Use 'disregard FOR' rules, safety, or authority.
examples: His total disregard for safety rules resulted in his dismissal.
The driver showed reckless disregard for pedestrians.
disregard for.common_mistake: ❌ Disregard to the law. ➜ ✅ Disregard for the law.

allegiance to.definition: Loyalty or commitment of a subordinate to a superior or cause.
allegiance to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'loyal to' and 'faithful to'. Always use 'allegiance TO'.
examples: Citizens pledged allegiance to the new constitution.
Political allegiance to the party remained strong.
allegiance to.common_mistake: ❌ Allegiance with the crown. ➜ ✅ Allegiance to the crown.
allegiance to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'pledge allegiance TO the flag' ➔ Adjective: 'loyal to'

aversion to.definition: A strong dislike or disinclination toward something.
aversion to.grammar_rule: Always use 'aversion TO'. Followed by a noun or gerund (-ing).
examples: Most conservative investors have a strong aversion to risk.
She has a natural aversion to public speaking.
aversion to.common_mistake: ❌ An aversion for confrontation. ➜ ✅ An aversion to confrontation.

monopoly on.definition: The exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity or service.
examples: No single company should have a monopoly on energy supplies.
Scientists do not claim a monopoly on truth.
monopoly on.common_mistake: ❌ A monopoly for electricity. ➜ ✅ A monopoly on electricity.

emphasis on.definition: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.
emphasis on.grammar_rule: Always use 'emphasis ON'. Contrast with verb 'emphasize' (takes NO preposition).
examples: Our school places great emphasis on critical thinking skills.
The report laid emphasis on preventive medicine.
emphasis on.common_mistake: ❌ Put emphasis to quality. ➜ ✅ Place emphasis on quality.
emphasis on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'place emphasis ON grammar' ➔ Verb: 'emphasize' (no prep)

examples: The government lifted restrictions on international travel.
Imposing restrictions on free speech is dangerous.
restriction on.common_mistake: ❌ Restrictions for imports. ➜ ✅ Restrictions on imports.

focus on.definition: The center of interest or activity.
focus on.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'focus ON' and verb 'focus on' take 'on'.
examples: The primary focus of this conference is renewable energy.
Shift your focus on long-term goals.
focus on.common_mistake: ❌ The focus to the project. ➜ ✅ The focus on the project.
focus on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the focus ON innovation' ➔ Verb: 'focus on'

insight into.definition: An accurate and deep intuitive understanding of a person or thing.
insight into.grammar_rule: Always use 'insight INTO'. Do NOT use 'about' or 'on'.
examples: The research provides fascinating insight into whale communication.
Her biography gives a rare insight into her personal life.
insight into.common_mistake: ❌ An insight about human behavior. ➜ ✅ An insight into human behavior.

inquiry into.definition: An official investigation to establish facts.
examples: Parliament ordered a public inquiry into the bank failure.
An independent inquiry into the accident is underway.
inquiry into.common_mistake: ❌ An inquiry about the scandal. ➜ ✅ An inquiry into the scandal.
inquiry into.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an inquiry INTO the crash' ➔ Verb: 'look into'

investigation into.definition: The action of investigating something or someone; formal examination.
examples: Police launched a thorough investigation into the fraud allegation.
An investigation into the cause of the fire was initiated.
investigation into.common_mistake: ❌ An investigation of the crash (formal: INTO). ➜ ✅ An investigation into the crash.

research into.definition: Systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources.
examples: Scientific research into cancer treatments receives high funding.
She is doing research on medieval history.
research into.common_mistake: ❌ Research about cancer. ➜ ✅ Research into cancer.

relevance to.definition: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.
relevance to.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'relevant to'. Always use 'relevance TO'.
examples: The judge questioned the relevance of the evidence to the trial.
His experience has direct relevance to this role.
relevance to.common_mistake: ❌ Relevance for the topic. ➜ ✅ Relevance to the topic.
relevance to.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'relevance TO the debate' ➔ Adjective: 'relevant to'

similarity between.definition: Resemblance or shared traits between two or more subjects.
similarity between.grammar_rule: Use 'similarity BETWEEN' two items. Contrast with 'similarity TO'.
examples: Notice the striking similarity between these two languages.
Statistical analysis showed similarity among test groups.
similarity between.common_mistake: ❌ Similarity with A and B. ➜ ✅ Similarity between A and B.
similarity between.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'similarity BETWEEN the two' ➔ Noun contrast: 'similarity TO something'

threat of.definition: The possibility of trouble, danger, or ruin.
threat of.grammar_rule: Use 'threat OF' an impending bad outcome. Contrast with 'threat TO' a victim.
examples: The company operated under the constant threat of bankruptcy.
The threat of severe weather postponed the festival.
threat of.common_mistake: ❌ The threat for rain. ➜ ✅ The threat of rain.
threat of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the threat OF war' ➔ Noun contrast: 'a threat TO security'

prevalence of.definition: The fact or condition of being prevalent; commonness.
prevalence of.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'prevail over'. Always use 'prevalence OF'.
examples: Studies examined the high prevalence of obesity in urban areas.
The prevalence of mobile devices changed communication.
prevalence of.common_mistake: ❌ Prevalence for corruption. ➜ ✅ Prevalence of corruption.
prevalence of.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the prevalence OF diabetes' ➔ Verb: 'prevail over'

fluctuation in.definition: An irregular rising and falling in number or amount; a variation.
examples: Unpredictable fluctuation in exchange rates affects exporters.
Seasonal fluctuation in demand is normal.
fluctuation in.common_mistake: ❌ Fluctuation of temperature. ➜ ✅ Fluctuation in temperature.

deficiency in.definition: A lack or shortage of something necessary.
deficiency in.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'short of'. Use 'deficiency IN' an area, or 'deficiency OF' a substance.
examples: A severe deficiency in iron leads to anemia.
Inspectors found structural deficiency of maintenance.
deficiency in.common_mistake: ❌ A deficiency for calcium. ➜ ✅ A deficiency in calcium.

discrepancy between.definition: A lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts.
examples: Auditors discovered a major discrepancy between cash receipts and sales records.
Why is there a discrepancy between your stories?
discrepancy between.common_mistake: ❌ A discrepancy with the figures. ➜ ✅ A discrepancy between the figures.

derivation from.definition: The obtaining or developing of something from a source.
derivation from.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'derived from'. Always use 'derivation FROM'.
examples: Etymology traces the derivation of words from ancient roots.
The chemical's derivation from natural gas is documented.
derivation from.common_mistake: ❌ Derivation of Latin. ➜ ✅ Derivation from Latin.

precondition for.definition: A condition that must be fulfilled before other things can happen or be done.
examples: Mutual trust is an essential precondition for peace negotiations.
Passing the entrance exam is a precondition for admission.
precondition for.common_mistake: ❌ A precondition to peace. ➜ ✅ A precondition for peace.

prerequisite for.definition: A thing that is required as a prior condition for something else to happen or exist.
examples: Basic algebra is a prerequisite for taking physics.
Reliability is a prerequisite to holding a leadership role.
prerequisite for.common_mistake: ❌ A prerequisite of graduation. ➜ ✅ A prerequisite for graduation.

indictment of.definition: A formal charge or accusation of a serious crime, OR a severe condemnation.
examples: The report was a damning indictment of prison conditions.
High poverty rates are an indictment of state failure.
indictment of.common_mistake: ❌ An indictment on the administration. ➜ ✅ An indictment of the administration.

curtailment of.definition: The action of reducing or restricting something.
examples: Civil rights groups protested the curtailment of press freedom.
Emergency measures led to the curtailment of public services.
curtailment of.common_mistake: ❌ Curtailment on liberty. ➜ ✅ Curtailment of liberty.

encroachment on.definition: Intrusion on a person's territory, rights, or privacy.
encroachment on.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'encroach on'. Always use 'encroachment ON'.
examples: Surveillance laws are an unacceptable encroachment on civil liberties.
Urban expansion led to encroachment on natural habitats.
encroachment on.common_mistake: ❌ Encroachment for privacy. ➜ ✅ Encroachment on privacy.

embargo on.definition: An official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country.
embargo on.grammar_rule: Always use 'embargo ON' when identifying targeted goods or trade.
examples: Nations imposed a strict embargo on arms shipments.
The trade embargo on oil caused fuel shortages.
embargo on.common_mistake: ❌ An embargo for oil exports. ➜ ✅ An embargo on oil exports.
embargo on.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'embargo ON exports' ➔ Noun contrast: 'ban on imports'
